youtube.aciklama: In the gaps-in-noise test (GIN), gaps of 2 to 20 milliseconds are placed in six-second segments of noise; in normal adults the approximate threshold is about 5 milliseconds. Because gap detection in broadband noise also uses high-frequency information, the threshold may be longer in a person with high-frequency hearing loss; so temporal tests are interpreted together with pure tone thresholds.
